The Hydrologic Cycle; The Hydrology of Runoff

Infiltration enters rock/soil through cracks or pores; runoff is precipitation flowing over land plus near-surface infiltrated water that returns to the surface. Climate controls the partition among evaporation, infiltration, and runoff.
Use textbook’s broad runoff definition; avoid treating all infiltrated water as permanently removed from runoff.
Lakes, artificial reservoirs and wetlands store high inflows and release water during dry periods, smoothing runoff variability.

The Hydrology of Groundwater; The Groundwater Table; Balancing Recharge and Discharge

Recent precipitation infiltrates to form meteoric groundwater. Recharge is infiltration into a subsurface formation; discharge is groundwater movement to the surface (evaporation, springs, wells, or streams). Balanced recharge/discharge maintains reservoir size and water-table elevation.
Groundwater 1.05% of all water (Figure 17.1). Chapter text later says ~29% of fresh water (PDF 1675); see conflict.
